WorkspaceOrchestrator.createWorkspace(): calls errorLogManager?.append() on clone failure with source='clone', operation='workspace-setup', context={ProjectId, WorkspaceId, RepositoryId}. Error message is the already-sanitised string from stripEmbeddedCredentials().

comments.note: All three orchestrators follow the same optional-injection pattern cleanly. The use of optional chaining (this.errorLogManager?.append(...)) keeps the zero-injection path fully allocation-free and makes the intent self-documenting.

BranchOrchestrator.switchBranches() has a note in its JSDoc that it does not validate project/workspace existence before iterating — error only surfaces at workspaceManager.update() at the end. This is pre-existing design debt unrelated to this WP, but worth noting for future review.

The catch-block in BranchOrchestrator.switchBranches() uses '(err as Error).message' for the error message — this is consistent with the existing code pattern. However, if err is not an Error instance (e.g. a string throw), the message would be undefined. The pre-existing pattern is retained here intentionally.

comments.note: All three orchestrators follow the identical optional-injection pattern (errorLogManager?: ErrorLogManager, optional chaining on append). The pattern is consistent, self-documenting, and allocation-free when the manager is not provided.

If errorLogManager.append() itself throws (e.g. disk full when writing error-log.json), the exception will propagate out of the Promise.all callback in createWorkspace/addRepositoryToProject/switchBranches, converting a partial-failure into a full rejection. Since a disk error at logging time is unlikely to be recoverable, this behaviour is acceptable, but callers should be aware that errorLogManager exceptions are not swallowed.

In BranchOrchestrator.switchBranches(), the non-zero exit code failure path and the catch path are mutually exclusive — no double-logging can occur for a single repository operation. The fallback message ('git exited with code N') correctly handles empty stderr.

comments.note: All three orchestrators follow an identical, allocation-free optional-injection pattern (errorLogManager?: ErrorLogManager, optional chaining on append). The symmetry makes the pattern discoverable and safe to copy for future orchestrators.

append() is synchronous and its return value (the constructed ErrorLogEntry) is correctly discarded at all call sites — callers do not need the stamped entry. The absence of await is intentional and correct.

BranchOrchestrator.switchBranches() correctly handles two distinct failure paths (non-zero exit code and thrown exception) as separate, mutually-exclusive error log entries. No double-logging can occur for a single repository operation.

[documentation-forward] The JSDoc for createWorkspace(), addRepositoryToProject(), and switchBranches() does not mention that if errorLogManager.append() itself throws (e.g. disk full writing error-log.json), that exception will propagate out of the Promise.all callback and convert a partial-failure into a full rejection. Add a @remarks or @throws note to each method so callers are aware that logging exceptions are not swallowed.
